description: Sleep hygiene and management strategies for menopause-related sleep problems

entries.title: Sleep Hygiene Basics
entries.description: Foundational practices for better sleep during menopause
entries.content: Good sleep hygiene - habits and practices that promote quality sleep - is essential during menopause when sleep is often disrupted by night sweats, insomnia, and hormonal changes. Establishing consistent routines and optimizing your sleep environment can significantly improve sleep quality.
key_practices: Maintain consistent sleep schedule (same bedtime and wake time daily, even weekends)
Create relaxing bedtime routine (30-60 minutes before bed)
Make bedroom dark (blackout curtains, eye mask)
Keep bedroom quiet (white noise machine if needed)
Reserve bed for sleep and sex only (not work, TV, phone)
Limit screen time 1-2 hours before bed (blue light disrupts sleep)
Avoid large meals close to bedtime
Limit fluids before bed to reduce nighttime bathroom trips

entries.title: Managing Night Sweats for Better Sleep
entries.description: Strategies to minimize sleep disruption from night sweats
entries.content: Night sweats are one of the most disruptive menopausal symptoms. These strategies can help minimize their impact on sleep quality.
strategies: Place cold packs under pillow, flip to cool side
Shower before bed to lower body temperature
Avoid triggers before bed (alcohol, spicy foods, hot drinks)
Consider medical treatment (HRT, gabapentin, other medications)
entries.medical_options: If night sweats severely disrupt sleep, discuss HRT or medications like gabapentin with doctor

entries.title: Caffeine and Alcohol Management
entries.description: How caffeine and alcohol affect sleep during menopause
entries.content: Caffeine and alcohol can significantly disrupt sleep, especially during menopause when sleep is already compromised. Managing intake, particularly timing, can improve sleep quality.
caffeine: Avoid caffeine after noon (or earlier if very sensitive)
Remember hidden sources: tea, soda, chocolate, some medications
Caffeine has 6-hour half-life (stays in system long time)
Can trigger hot flashes and worsen sleep
alcohol: While alcohol may help you fall asleep, it disrupts sleep quality and causes early waking
Triggers hot flashes and night sweats

entries.title: Relaxation Techniques for Sleep
entries.description: Methods to calm mind and body for better sleep
entries.content: Relaxation techniques can help calm an anxious or racing mind, reduce stress, and prepare your body for sleep. These are particularly helpful during menopause when anxiety and stress can worsen sleep problems.
techniques: Deep breathing exercises (4-7-8 breathing, diaphragmatic breathing)
Progressive muscle relaxation (tense and release muscle groups)
Listening to calming music or sleep sounds
Journaling to clear mind of worries
Warm bath (not hot, which can trigger hot flash)
entries.timing: Practice 30-60 minutes before bed as part of bedtime routine

entries.title: When to Seek Help for Sleep Problems
entries.description: Signs that sleep problems need medical attention
entries.content: While some sleep disruption is common during menopause, persistent or severe sleep problems warrant medical attention. Chronic poor sleep affects health, mood, and quality of life.
seek_help_if: Sleep problems persist despite good sleep hygiene
Daytime functioning is significantly impaired (fatigue, concentration, mood)
Falling asleep while driving or during activities
Loud snoring or gasping during sleep (could indicate sleep apnea)
Severe insomnia (difficulty falling or staying asleep most nights)
treatment_options: Treat underlying causes (night sweats with HRT or medications)
Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I) - highly effective
Sleep study if sleep apnea suspected
